question: What was the Council of Nicaea (325 AD) primarily called to address?

choices.A: Arianism — the heresy that the Son is a created being, not co-equal and co-eternal with the Father
choices.B: The date of Easter and whether it should follow the Jewish calendar
choices.C: The question of which books belong in the biblical canon
choices.D: The establishment of papal authority over all Eastern bishops

teaching.title: Council of Nicaea (325) and Arianism
teaching.body: Arius of Alexandria (~256-336) taught that the Son was the highest created being — 'there was when he was not' — making him subordinate to and ontologically different from the Father. This threatened the coherence of Christian salvation (only God can save). Emperor Constantine convened the First Ecumenical Council at Nicaea (325), which condemned Arianism and defined the Son as 'homoousios' (consubstantial, of the same essence) with the Father. The Nicene Creed's phrase 'God from God, Light from Light, true God from true God, begotten not made, consubstantial with the Father' directly refutes Arianism.
